claim: CLC-7 is a chloride-proton exchanger that plays critical roles in lysosomal homeostasis and bone regeneration.
source: The chloride-proton exchanger CLC-7 plays critical roles in lysosomal homeostasis and bone regeneration and its mutation can lead to osteopetrosis, lysosomal storage disease and neurological disorders.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general characterization of CLC-7's function, supported by the broader literature context.

claim: Mutations in CLC-7 can lead to osteopetrosis, lysosomal storage disease and neurological disorders.
source: The chloride-proton exchanger CLC-7 plays critical roles in lysosomal homeostasis and bone regeneration and its mutation can lead to osteopetrosis, lysosomal storage disease and neurological disorders.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: CLC-7 requires OSTM1 for stability and activity in lysosomes and the ruffled border of osteoclasts.
source: In lysosomes and the ruffled border of osteoclasts, CLC-7 requires a β-subunit, OSTM1, for stability and activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations (Lange et al., 2006; Leisle et al., 2011) in the introduction.

claim: Electron cryomicroscopy structures of CLC-7 in occluded states were determined at resolutions up to 2.8 Å.
source: Here, we present electron cryomicroscopy structures of CLC-7 in occluded states by itself and in complex with OSTM1, determined at resolutions up to 2.8 Å.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Table 1 and the results section.

claim: The luminal surface of CLC-7 is entirely covered by a dimer of heavily glycosylated and disulfide-bonded OSTM1 in the complex.
source: In the complex, the luminal surface of CLC-7 is entirely covered by a dimer of the heavily glycosylated and disulfide-bonded OSTM1, which serves to protect CLC-7 from the degradative environment of the lysosomal lumen.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 5 and Figure 6.

claim: OSTM1 serves to protect CLC-7 from the degradative environment of the lysosomal lumen.
source: In the complex, the luminal surface of CLC-7 is entirely covered by a dimer of the heavily glycosylated and disulfide-bonded OSTM1, which serves to protect CLC-7 from the degradative environment of the lysosomal lumen.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural data showing OSTM1 coverage and glycosylation.

claim: OSTM1 binding does not induce large-scale rearrangements of CLC-7.
source: OSTM1 binding does not induce large-scale rearrangements of CLC-7, but does have minor effects on the conformation of the ion-conduction pathway, potentially contributing to its regulatory role.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparison data in Figure 7.

claim: OSTM1 binding has minor effects on the conformation of the ion-conduction pathway of CLC-7.
source: OSTM1 binding does not induce large-scale rearrangements of CLC-7, but does have minor effects on the conformation of the ion-conduction pathway, potentially contributing to its regulatory role.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by structural comparison data in Figure 7.

claim: CLC-7 is expressed in the lysosome and the resorption lacuna of osteoclasts.
source: CLC-7 is a member of the CLC family of chloride (Cl-) channels and chloride (Cl-)/proton (H+) transporters and is expressed in the lysosome and the resorption lacuna of osteoclasts (Graves et al., 2008; Ishida et al., 2013; Kornak et al., 2001; Weinert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CLC-7 catalyzes the uptake of two Cl- ions for each H+ released using the large pH gradient.
source: In the membranes of these acidic compartments, CLC-7 uses the large pH gradient to catalyze the uptake of two Cl- ions for each H+ released (Graves et al., 2008; Leisle et al., 2011; Ludwig et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Dysfunction of CLC-7 is associated with dysregulation of ion and pH homeostasis of the lysosome and the resorption lacuna.
source: Dysfunction of CLC-7 is associated with dysregulation of ion and pH homoeostasis of the lysosome and the resorption lacuna (Graves et al., 2008; Ishida et al., 2013; Kasper et al., 2005; Kornak et al., 2001; Lange et al., 2006; Undiagnosed Diseases Network et al., 2019; Steinberg et al., 2010; Weinert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Osteopetrosis is the most common disease associated with CLC-7 mutation, with more than 50 distinct pathogenic mutations identified.
source: In particular, osteopetrosis, a disease characterized by dense and brittle bones, is the most common disease associated with CLC-7 mutation, with more than 50 distinct pathogenic mutations identified to date (Chalhoub et al., 2003; Cleiren et al., 2001; Kasper et al., 2005; Kornak et al., 2001; Lange et al., 2006; Sartelet et al., 2014; Schulz et al., 2010; Weinert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The gating glutamate (Glugate) in CLC transporters is proposed to oscillate between at least four different conformations.
source: Within the Cl--conduction pathway, the gating glutamate (Glugate) that is conserved in CLC transporters is proposed to oscillate between at least four different conformations (Chavan et al., 2020; Dutzler et al., 2002; Dutzler et al., 2003; Feng et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The movement and changes in the protonation state of Glugate are coupled to the binding and release of Cl- ions in the external and central binding sites.
source: The movement and changes in the protonation state of Glugate are coupled to the binding and release of Cl- ions in the highly conserved external and central binding sites (Picollo et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The conserved internal glutamate (Gluin) is dispensable for coupled transport in CLC transporters.
source: This conserved Gluin is dispensable for coupled transport and water molecules has been proposed to mediate H+ transport through the hydrophobic gap (Feng et al., 2010; Han et al., 2014; Wang and Voth, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Water molecules have been proposed to mediate H+ transport through the hydrophobic gap in CLC transporters.
source: This conserved Gluin is dispensable for coupled transport and water molecules has been proposed to mediate H+ transport through the hydrophobic gap (Feng et al., 2010; Han et al., 2014; Wang and Voth, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CLC-7 and OSTM1 co-localize in lysosomes and the ruffled border of osteoclasts.
source: CLC-7 and OSTM1 co-localize in lysosomes and the ruffled border of osteoclasts (Lange et al., 2006; Leisle et al., 2011; Schulz et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: CLC-7 and OSTM1 stabilize the expression of one another and are both required for Cl-/H+ exchange.
source: There, CLC-7 and OSTM1 stabilize the expression of one another and are both required for Cl-/H+ exchange (Lange et al., 2006; Leisle et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: OSTM1 is predicted to be a glycosylated, single-pass transmembrane protein.
source: OSTM1 is predicted to be a glycosylated, single-pass transmembrane protein and mutations in OSTM1, like mutations in CLC-7, can lead to osteopetrosis and neurodegeneration in humans and mice (Chalhoub et al., 2003; Kasper et al., 2005; Kornak et al., 2001; Lange et al., 2006; Majumdar et al., 2011; Pressey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Mutations in OSTM1 can lead to osteopetrosis and neurodegeneration in humans and mice.
source: OSTM1 is predicted to be a glycosylated, single-pass transmembrane protein and mutations in OSTM1, like mutations in CLC-7, can lead to osteopetrosis and neurodegeneration in humans and mice (Chalhoub et al., 2003; Kasper et al., 2005; Kornak et al., 2001; Lange et al., 2006; Majumdar et al., 2011; Pressey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Chicken CLC-7 (ggCLC-7) and human CLC-7 are 86.4% identical.
source: Full-length chicken CLC-7 (ggCLC-7) and human CLC-7, which are 86.4% identical, were expressed in HEK293S GnTI- cells as mEGFP-fusions, purified to homogeneity in the detergent lauryl maltose neopentyl glycol (LMNG), cholesterol hemisuccinate (CHS), 150 mM KCl and 50 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, and analyzed by cryo-EM.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the protein preparation.

claim: Vitrified human CLC-7 transporters displayed a strongly preferred orientation that prevented three-dimensional structure determination.
source: Vitrified human CLC-7 transporters displayed a strongly preferred orientation that was confirmed by two-dimensional classification (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). Because of the very limited views of the transporter, we were not able to reconstruct a three-dimensional density map of human CLC-7.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The structure of dimeric ggCLC-7 was determined at a resolution of 2.9 Å.
source: Reconstruction of these particle images with twofold symmetry imposed yielded a structure of dimeric ggCLC-7 at a resolution of 2.9 Å that enabled model building (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by Table 1 and figures.

claim: Each protomer of dimeric ggCLC-7 contains a transmembrane domain composed of 18-transmembrane helices.
source: Each protomer of dimeric ggCLC-7 contains a transmembrane domain composed of 18-transmembrane helices and a cytoplasmic domain composed of an N-terminal domain and two C-terminal cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) domains (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Each protomer of dimeric ggCLC-7 contains a cytoplasmic domain composed of an N-terminal domain and two C-terminal CBS domains.
source: Each protomer of dimeric ggCLC-7 contains a transmembrane domain composed of 18-transmembrane helices and a cytoplasmic domain composed of an N-terminal domain and two C-terminal cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) domains (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The ggCLC-7 dimer interface is approximately 3700 Å2.
source: Both the transmembrane and cytosolic domains contribute to the large (~3700 Å2) ggCLC-7 dimer interface (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The transmembrane domain of ggCLC-7 adopts the canonical CLC architecture.
source: The transmembrane domain of ggCLC-7 adopts the canonical CLC architecture with each protomer possessing discrete ion permeation pathways that extend from the cytosol to the lysosomal lumen (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In ggCLC-7, constrictions too narrow to accommodate Cl- ions exist on both ends of the Cl--conduction pathway.
source: In the present conformation of ggCLC-7, constrictions too narrow to accommodate Cl- ions exist on both ends of the Cl--conduction pathway (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: On the cytosolic side of the ggCLC-7 Cl--conduction pathway, the side chains of Ser200, Tyr501 and Tyr598 form a constriction with a minimum radius of 0.6 Å.
source: On the cytosolic side of the pathway between the central and internal Cl--binding sites, the side chains of Ser200, Tyr501 and Tyr598 form a constriction with a minimum radius of 0.6 Å (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The luminal side of the ggCLC-7 Cl--conduction pathway contains two constrictions.
source: The luminal side of the Cl--conduction pathway contains two additional constrictions (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The first luminal constriction in ggCLC-7 has a minimum radius of 0.7 Å and is formed by Glu243, Ile511 and the backbone of Lys242 and Glu243.
source: The first constriction, which has a minimum radius of 0.7 Å is immediately adjacent to the external Cl--binding site and is formed by the side chains of Glu243, Ile511 and the backbone of Lys242 and Glu243.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The second luminal constriction in ggCLC-7 has a minimum radius of 1.1 Å and is formed by Lys242, Glu467 and the backbone of Gly241.
source: The second constriction (1.1 Å minimum radius) is at the luminal entrance and is formed by the side chains of Lys242, Glu467 and the backbone of Gly241.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The three constrictions in ggCLC-7 yield an occluded state for the transporter, sealing off the external and central Cl--binding sites from the cytosol and the lysosomal lumen.
source: Together the three constrictions yield an occluded state for the transporter, sealing off the external and central Cl--binding sites from the cytosol and the lysosomal lumen.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: In ggCLC-7, the Glugate (Glu243) adopts the 'up' conformation.
source: In ggCLC-7, the Glugate (Glu243) adopts the 'up' conformation, where it participates in establishing one of the luminal constrictions (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Non-protein densities attributed to Cl- ions were resolved at the external, central and internal Cl--binding sites in ggCLC-7.
source: Within the Cl--conduction pathway, non-protein densities that we attributed to Cl- ions were resolved at the external, central and internal Cl--binding sites (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The external Cl- site in ggCLC-7 is formed by the backbone nitrogens of Glu243 and Gly244 on helix αF and Phe510 and Ile511 on helix αO.
source: The external Cl- site is formed by the backbone nitrogens of Glu243 and Gly244 on helix αF and Phe510 and Ile511 on helix αO.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The intensity of the external Cl--binding site in ggCLC-7 is the strongest of the three Cl--binding sites, suggesting a high Cl- occupancy.
source: The intensity of the external Cl--binding site (~14 σ) is the strongest of the three Cl--binding sites and is nearly equivalent to that of backbone atoms of nearby residues, suggesting a high Cl- occupancy.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the density map.

claim: The central Cl- site in ggCLC-7 is formed by the side chains of Ser200 and Tyr598 and the backbone nitrogens of Val509 and Phe510.
source: The density for the central Cl- site has a slightly lower intensity (~12 σ) and is formed by the side chains of the highly conserved Ser200 from helix αD and Tyr598 on helix αS and the backbone nitrogens of Val509 and Phe510 of helix αN.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The internal Cl--binding site in ggCLC-7 is formed by the backbone nitrogens of Ser200 and Gly201 and the side chain of Gln204.
source: The internal Cl--binding site, which is located in a solvent-exposed vestibule on the cytoplasmic side of the transporter, has the lowest intermediate intensity (~8 σ) and is formed by the backbone nitrogens of Ser200 and Gly201 and the side chain of Gln204, all on helix αD.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The relative intensities of the three Cl--binding sites in ggCLC-7 are consistent with the central and external binding sites having much higher affinity for Cl- ions than the internal site.
source: The relative intensities of the three Cl--binding sites are consistent with structural and biochemical studies performed with E. coli CLC1 (ecCLC) that showed that the central and external binding sites have much higher affinity for Cl- ions than the internal site (Lobet and Dutzler, 2006; Picollo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: In the ggCLC-7 structure, Gluin (Glu310) is located more than 15 Å away from Glugate.
source: In the ggCLC-7 structure, Gluin (Glu310) on helix αG is located more than 15 Å away from Glugate, where it extends into a solvent filled cavity between the transmembrane and cytosolic domains that is continuous with the cytosol (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: Several non-protein densities were resolved within the hydrophobic gap between Glugate and Gluin in ggCLC-7 that were tentatively modeled as water molecules.
source: Within the loosely packed hydrophobic gap between Glugate and Gluin, several non-protein densities were resolved that we have tentatively modeled as water molecules (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Water molecules have previously been detected within the hydrophobic gap in structures and molecular dynamics simulations of CLC transporters.
source: Water molecules have previously been detected within the hydrophobic gap in structures and in molecular dynamics simulations of CLC transporters and have been proposed to serve as a proton-conducting water-wire (Chavan et al., 2020; Han et al., 2014; Leisle et al., 2020; Wang and Voth, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with supporting citations.

claim: In ggCLC-7, the water molecules in the hydrophobic gap can access the Cl--conduction pathway through an opening with a minimum radius of ~1.4 Å between Gly244, Phe297 and Phe510.
source: In ggCLC-7, the water molecules in the hydrophobic gap can access the Cl--conduction pathway through an opening with a minimum radius of ~1.4 Å between Gly244, Phe297 and Phe510 (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The hydrophobic gap in ggCLC-7 is sealed near Gluin by a 1.0 Å constriction formed by Ile202, Phe306 and Met558.
source: However, the pathway is not continuous with the cytosol as the hydrophobic gap is sealed near Gluin by a 1.0 Å constriction formed Ile202, Phe306 and Met558.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: A conformational change may occur during the transport cycle of ggCLC-7 to open the constrictions and allow protons to pass through the hydrophobic gap.
source: It is possible that a similar conformational change may occur during the transport cycle of ggCLC-7 to open the constrictions and allow protons to pass through the hydrophobic gap.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as speculation based on comparison with other CLC structures.

claim: The N-terminal domain of ggCLC-7 is comprised of a 14-amino acid extended segment and helix αA.
source: The N-terminal domain, which has not been resolved in previous CLC structures, is comprised of a 14-amino acid extended segment and helix αA that are well-defined in the ggCLC-7 density map (Figure 3B and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3B and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The N-terminal domain of ggCLC-7 has not been resolved in previous CLC structures.
source: The N-terminal domain, which has not been resolved in previous CLC structures, is comprised of a 14-amino acid extended segment and helix αA that are well-defined in the ggCLC-7 density map (Figure 3B and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The N-terminal domain of ggCLC-7 is positioned at the center of the three-way interface between the transmembrane domain, CBS1 and CBS2.
source: The extended segment is positioned at the center of the three-way interface between the transmembrane domain, CBS1 and CBS2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The N-terminal domain of ggCLC-7 forms a larger interface with the transmembrane domain than either of the CBS domains.
source: Indeed, the N-terminal domain forms a larger interface with the transmembrane domain than either of the CBS domains.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: A large non-protein density in a groove between the two CBS domains of ggCLC-7 was modeled as a Mg2+-bound ATP.
source: Immediately adjacent to the N-terminal domain in a groove between the two CBS domains is a large density that cannot be attributed to the protein (Figure 3C). We modeled this non-protein density as a Mg2+-bound ATP based on its shape and a comparison with the ATP-bound structure of the isolated CBS domains of CLC-5 (Meyer et al., 2007; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: No nucleotides were added during the 30-hour purification of ggCLC-7, so any ATP present must have been co-purified with the transporter.
source: Notably, no nucleotides were added during the 30-hour purification of ggCLC-7 so any ATP present must have been co-purified with the transporter.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: In the ggCLC-7 structure, the transporter forms multiple interactions with all three components of the ATP molecule.
source: In the ggCLC-7 structure, the transporter forms multiple interactions with all three components of the ATP molecule (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The adenine base of ATP in ggCLC-7 is sandwiched between the side chains of His654 on CBS1 and Met778 on CBS2.
source: The adenine base of the ATP is sandwiched between the side chains of His654 on CBS1, with which it forms π-stacking interactions, and Met778 on CBS2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The adenine base of ATP in ggCLC-7 forms polar interactions with the side-chain oxygen and backbone nitrogen of Thr632 and the backbone nitrogen of Gly656.
source: The adenine base also forms polar interactions with the side-chain oxygen and backbone nitrogen of Thr632 and the backbone nitrogen of Gly656 that contribute to the specificity for adenine nucleotides (Meyer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The ribose sugar of ATP in ggCLC-7 forms polar interactions with side chains of Ser628 and Asp783.
source: The ribose sugar forms polar interactions with side chains of Ser628 and Asp783.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The α-phosphate of ATP in ggCLC-7 interacts with the side chain of His654 and the backbone oxygen of Asn653 of CBS1, and the side chain of Lys782 of CBS2.
source: The α-phosphate interacts with the side chain of His654 and the backbone oxygen of Asn653 of CBS1, the side chain of Lys782 of CBS2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: A Mg2+ ion coordinating the α- and β-phosphate of ATP in ggCLC-7 is partially coordinated by Glu91 of the N-terminal domain.
source: Coordinating the α- and β-phosphate is a Mg2+ that is partially coordinated by Glu91 of the N-terminal domain.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The β-phosphate of ATP in ggCLC-7 interacts with the side chain of Asn655 and the backbone oxygen of His654 of CBS1 and the side chain of His765 of CBS2.
source: Additionally, the β-phosphate also interacts with the side chain of Asn655 and the backbone oxygen of His654 of CBS1 and the side chain of His765 of CBS2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The γ-phosphate of ATP in ggCLC-7 interacts with the side chain and backbone nitrogen of Ser92 of the N-terminal domain and the side chain of Arg764 of CBS2.
source: The γ-phosphate interacts with the side chain and backbone nitrogen of Ser92 of the N-terminal domain and the side chain of Arg764 of CBS2.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The numerous interactions between ATP and ggCLC-7 and the slow-off rate of ATP during purification are consistent with ATP binding to ggCLC-7 with high affinity.
source: Together, the numerous interactions between ATP and ggCLC-7 and the slow-off rate of ATP during the purification are consistent with ATP binding to ggCLC-7 with high affinity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The ATP-binding site in ggCLC-7 shares many features with the ATP-binding site in the isolated CBS domains of CLC-5, including the coordination of the adenine base and the ribose sugar.
source: The ATP-binding site in ggCLC-7 shares many features with the ATP-binding site resolved in the structure of the isolated CBS domains of CLC-5, including the coordination of the adenine base and the ribose sugar (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; Meyer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The major differences between the ATP interactions of human CLC-5 and ggCLC-7 are the additional interactions with the triphosphate group of ATP in ggCLC-7.
source: The major differences between the ATP interactions of human CLC-5 and ggCLC-7 are the additional interactions with the triphosphate group of ATP in ggCLC-7.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Both ATP and Mg2+ directly interact with the N-terminal domain of CLC-7.
source: In particular, both ATP and Mg2+ directly interact with the N-terminal domain of CLC-7 (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The N-terminal domain was not present in the CLC-5 CBS domain crystallization construct.
source: As the N-terminal domain was not present in the CLC-5 CBS domain crystallization construct (Meyer et al., 2007), such interactions were not previously identified.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Binding studies with the CLC-5 CBS domains found that ATP binds with an affinity of ~100 μM, similar to affinities measured for ADP and AMP.
source: Binding studies performed with the CLC-5 CBS domains found that ATP binds with an affinity of ~100 μM, similar to affinities measured for ADP and AMP (Meyer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The densities corresponding to the α-phosphate and γ-phosphate are nearly equivalent in the ggCLC-7 density map, indicating that ATP was the predominant species co-purified with transporter.
source: In contrast, the densities corresponding to the α-phosphate and γ-phosphate are nearly equivalent in the ggCLC-7 density map, indicating that ATP was predominant species co-purified with transporter (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The N-terminal domain resolved in the ggCLC-7 structure (residues 87–114) is conserved in human CLC-7 and human CLC-6.
source: Sequence alignment of ggCLC-7 with the nine human CLC proteins reveals the N-terminal domain resolved in the ggCLC-7 structure (residues 87–114) is conserved in human CLC-7 as well as the closely-related human CLC-6 transporter (45% identity).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Glu91 and Ser92, the residues that interact with the triphosphate group of ATP in ggCLC-7, are only conserved in CLC-6 and CLC-7.
source: Furthermore, Glu91 and Ser92, the residues that interact with the triphosphate group of ATP in ggCLC-7, are only conserved in CLC-6 and CLC-7, indicating that ATP binding may vary among CLC proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: ATP is speculated to be the preferred ligand for CLC-7.
source: We therefore speculate that ATP is the preferred ligand for CLC-7 and that further studies resolving the N-terminal domain of other CLC transporters will reveal to what extent CLC transporters bind specific adenine nucleotides.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as speculation.

claim: Non-protein densities that likely correspond to either ordered lipids or detergents were resolved around the periphery of the transmembrane domain of ggCLC-7.
source: Non-protein densities that likely correspond to either ordered lipids or detergents were resolved around the periphery of the transmembrane domain of ggCLC-7 (Figures 1A and 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figures 1A and 4A,B.

claim: One of the non-protein densities in ggCLC-7 was modeled as phosphoinositol-3-phosphate (PI3P).
source: Because it is difficult to distinguish lipids from detergents based on cryo-EM density maps alone, we were able to assign only one of the densities. The well-resolved head group allowed us to model the density as a phosphoinositol-3-phosphate (PI3P), which is a low-abundance constituent of lysosomal membranes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PI3P is a low-abundance constituent of lysosomal membranes.
source: The well-resolved head group allowed us to model the density as a phosphoinositol-3-phosphate (PI3P), which is a low-abundance constituent of lysosomal membranes (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: PI3P was co-purified with the ggCLC-7 transporter from the HEK293S GnTI- cell membranes.
source: Similar to ATP, PI3P was co-purified with the transporter from the HEK293S GnTI- cell membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The PI3P molecule in ggCLC-7 is located at the interface between the transmembrane domain and the cytosolic domain.
source: The PI3P molecule is located at the interface between the transmembrane domain and the cytosolic domain and interacts with residues from both domains.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: An amphipathic β-hairpin between helices αF and αG in ggCLC-7 surrounds the inositol phosphate head group and glycerol backbone of PI3P.
source: An amphipathic β-hairpin between helices αF and αG containing multiple positively charged residues surrounds the inositol phosphate head group and glycerol backbone, separating them from the rest of the membrane (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A–C.

claim: The PI3P head group in ggCLC-7 interacts with Lys213, Arg219 and Arg714, which coordinate the phosphate group at the 3 position of inositol ring.
source: The head group also interacts with Lys213, Arg219 and Arg714, which coordinate the phosphate group at the 3 position of inositol ring, and with Val218, Leu220, Val252, Ala255, Ser262, Thr263 and Lys281.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Two 8-carbon acyl chains were modeled into PI3P density in a groove on the surface of ggCLC-7 formed by helices αB, αE and αF.
source: Two 8-carbon acyl chains were modeled into PI3P density in a groove on the surface of the transporter formed by helices αB, αE and αF.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The elaborated loop between helices αF and αG present in ggCLC-7 is conserved in human CLC-7, CLC-6, and atCLC-a.
source: Among human CLCs, the elaborated loop between helices αF and αG present in ggCLC-7 is conserved in CLC-7 as well as CLC-6. The loop is also present in the vacuolar nitrate/H+ antiporter CLC-a from Arabidopsis thaliana (atCLC-a) (De Angeli et al., 2006; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a supporting citation and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Three positively charged residues within the β-hairpin of CLC-7, CLC-6, and atCLC-a may facilitate access of the negatively-charged lipid into the binding pocket.
